details.publicNotes:
A whittler's serpent is the inevitable manifestation of bardic magic combined with bardic instruments. Made up of the wood shavings that accumulate in the workshops of luthiers and reedmakers, the whittler's serpent is slowly animated by the power of music and song. As notes resonate through fallen whorls of wood, these remnants weave together into sinuous patterns of scales. A whittler's serpent starts off small, with a soft and breathy voice and only the knowledge of the tunes that animated it to life. As the years pass, it builds up a library of music and learns to improvise and accompany other performers. With no need to breathe, eat, or sleep, whittler's serpents are free to spend their every moment experiencing the sounds around them and seeking out new sources of music.

Many music shops and concert halls keep a whittler's serpent as a kind of mascot or pest control. These serpents are also favored companions of wandering bards and even spies, who value the clever creature's skill at reproducing conversations. However, those who enjoy a serpent's company must take care never to allow another whittler's serpent to approach. When two whitter's serpents meet, the result is often deadly. The larger serpent typically kills and consumes the smaller one, absorbing its victims' wood shavings and auditory memories alike. If this process happens enough times, the resulting serpent grows in size and intelligence, developing its own innate occult magic. Engineering this transformation is risky, however, as these stronger serpents tend to be cunning and bloodthirsty.

Musical Companion

Made from the wood shavings planed from many a lute and pipe, whittler's serpents have an instinctive affinity for the instruments from which they sprang. A whittler's serpent will sometimes develop a particular attachment to one of their sister instruments, following its owner whether the serpent is wanted or not. Sometimes a whittler's serpent will even stow away in order to stay with a beloved instrument, although finding one is easy: just strike up a tune and they can't resist singing along.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 3.5/7/13 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (piercing), perception item, skill items (Athletics, Intimidation, Performance, Stealth)

Eligible Imbued Properties bane, charisma, constitution, dexterity, energy resistant (sonic, vitality), mind, mind shield, music, sensory (darkvision), tangle shield, throwing, wild, wood

description.value: A whittler's serpent does not understand languages, but it can emulate speech, poetry, and music that it has heard, even producing instrumental sounds such as maracas, drums, or pipes. It instinctively accompanies nearby music. If it rolls a failure or critical failure on a check to Aid a Performance, it gets a success instead.

Trigger A creature attempts a melee attack roll against the whittler's serpent

Effect The whittler's serpent rattles its body in a sound reminiscent of a rattlesnake or a maraca, in an attempt to divert the attack and discourage further violence. The creature must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:17] save or become @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure).

Frequency Once every [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}

Effect The inspiration that drives bards and other entertainers is left as a remnant in the whittler's serpent. The whittler's serpent makes a bite Strike, rolling the attack twice and using the better result. The attack ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the target being @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} or hidden.
A whittler's serpent can [[/act feint skill=performance]] using Performance instead of Deception. The Feint gains the auditory trait and loses the mental trait.
